\section[perendiē]{perendiē — the day after tomorrow}

\label{lesson:LA-C163-perendie}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for before, then the Latin for to happen.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: perendiē}
\textbf{perendiē} — \textquotedblleft{}the day after tomorrow\textquotedblright{}. One day further on than \textbf{crās}: \textbf{Perendiē Rōmam ībō.} — \textquotedblleft{}The day after tomorrow I will go to Rome.\textquotedblright{} \textbf{ībō} is the future of \textbf{eō}.

\section[posteā]{posteā — afterwards, later}

\label{lesson:LA-C163-postea}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for to happen, then the Latin for the day after tomorrow.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: posteā}
\textbf{posteā} — \textquotedblleft{}afterwards, later\textquotedblright{}. It is \textbf{post}, \textquotedblleft{}after\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{eā}. \textbf{Posteā tē vidēbō.} — \textquotedblleft{}I will see you afterwards.\textquotedblright{} \textbf{vidēbō} is the future you met in \textbf{crās tē vidēbō}.

\section[cōnstituō, cōnstituere]{cōnstituō, cōnstituere — to decide, to set up}

\label{lesson:LA-C163-constituo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for afterwards, then the Latin for a plan; advice.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: cōnstituō, cōnstituere}
\textbf{cōnstituō, cōnstituere} — \textquotedblleft{}to decide, to set up\textquotedblright{}. Third-conjugation verbs, with a short \textbf{-ere}, make their future with \textbf{-am}, \textbf{-ēs}, \textbf{-et}: \textbf{Crās cōnstituam.} — \textquotedblleft{}I will decide tomorrow.\textquotedblright{} English \emph{constitute} and \emph{constitution} come from it.

\section[prōvideō, prōvidēre]{prōvideō, prōvidēre — to foresee, to provide for}

\label{lesson:LA-C163-provideo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for a plan; advice, then the Latin for to decide.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: prōvideō, prōvidēre}
\textbf{prōvideō, prōvidēre} — \textquotedblleft{}to foresee, to provide for\textquotedblright{}. It is \textbf{videō} with \textbf{prō}, \textquotedblleft{}ahead\textquotedblright{}: seeing a thing before it comes. Its future follows \textbf{vidēbō}: \textbf{prōvidēbō}. English \emph{provide} and \emph{provident} come from it.
